:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=\cos{t}, \quad y=\sin{t}, \qquad  0\leq t<2\pi,
$$

 calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$

![](images/2e/2ec95dd061fa6b7f09c9f899a1f6483b4ea7d5127372ddd6eefb74d6ed10c14c.png)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t) = -\sin{t}, \qquad y'(t)=\cos{t}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\cos t}{-\sin t} = -\cot t.
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,y=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,
$$

 calculate $\frac{dy}{dx}.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(\theta )=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{y}^{′}(\theta )=-5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{-5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }=-\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .
$$

The slope of the tangent to $C$ at time $t$ equals$\,$

The slope of the tangent to $C$ equals $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.$ To calculate this, we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

In parts 1 and 2, we found

$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{t}^{2}-2}{(\frac{5}{25+{t}^{2}})}=\frac{1}{5}({t}^{2}-2)({t}^{2}+25).
$$

$$

At the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =-\,\frac{3}{(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cot}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+1} \\  & =-\,\frac{3}{(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot 0+1} \\  & =-\,3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

For the parametric curve

$$
x=3t e^{3t},\quad y=5(t^2+2)e^{-3t},\quad -\infty<t<\infty,
$$

calculate $\frac{dy}{dx}$ as a function of $t$ for $t\ne - \frac{1}{3}.$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=$
{{field-1}}
inventory_only_records.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=3\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t\right)\right)e^{3t}+3t\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(e^{3t}\right)\right),\quad y'(t)=5\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t^2+2\right)\right)e^{-3t}+5(t^2+2)\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(e^{-3t}\right)\right)
$$

$$
x'(t)=3e^{3t}+ 3t(3e^{3t}),\quad y'(t)=5(2t)e^{-3t}+5(t^2+2)(-3e^{-3t})
$$

$$
x'(t)=3(1+3t)e^{3t},\quad y'(t)=5(2t-3(t^2+2))e^{-3t}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{5(2t-3(t^2+2))e^{-3t}}{3(1+3t)e^{3t}}=\frac{5(2t-3(t^2+2))}{3(1+3t)}e^{-6t}.
$$

This derivative is defined for $t\ne - \frac{1}{3}.$

inventory_only_records.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve

$$
x=\frac{1t}{t+1},\quad y=\frac{1t^2}{t+4},\quad t>0,
$$

calculate $\frac{dy}{dx}$ as a function of $t.$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=$
{{field-1}}
inventory_only_records.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=\frac{1\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t\right)\right)(t+1)-1t\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t+1\right)\right)}{(t+1)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{1\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t^2\right)\right)(t+4)-1t^2\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t+4\right)\right)}{(t+4)^2}
$$

$$
x'(t)=\frac{1(t+1)-1t(1)}{(t+1)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{2t(t+4)-1t^2(1)}{(t+4)^2}
$$

$$
x'(t)=\frac{1t+1-1t}{(t+1)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{2t^2+8t-1t^2}{(t+4)^2}
$$

$$
x'(t)=\frac{1}{(t+1)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{1t^2+8t}{(t+4)^2}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{1t^2+8t}{(t+4)^2}}{\frac{1}{(t+1)^2}}=\frac{(1t^2+8t)(t+1)^2}{1(t+4)^2}.
$$

inventory_only_records.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve

$$
x=\frac{4t}{t+2},\quad y=\frac{4t^2}{t+1},\quad t>0,
$$

calculate $\frac{dy}{dx}$ as a function of $t.$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=$
{{field-1}}
inventory_only_records.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=\frac{4\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t\right)\right)(t+2)-4t\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t+2\right)\right)}{(t+2)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{4\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t^2\right)\right)(t+1)-4t^2\left(\frac{d}{dt}\left(t+1\right)\right)}{(t+1)^2}
$$

$$
x'(t)=\frac{4(t+2)-4t(1)}{(t+2)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{8t(t+1)-4t^2(1)}{(t+1)^2}
$$

$$
x'(t)=\frac{4t+8-4t}{(t+2)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{8t^2+8t-4t^2}{(t+1)^2}
$$

$$
x'(t)=\frac{8}{(t+2)^2},\quad y'(t)=\frac{4t^2+8t}{(t+1)^2}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{4t^2+8t}{(t+1)^2}}{\frac{8}{(t+2)^2}}=\frac{(4t^2+8t)(t+2)^2}{8(t+1)^2}.
$$
